extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and scholars interested in Sigmund Freud and psychoanalysis
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive encyclopedic / wiki-style article summarizing Sigmund Freud's life, major works, intellectual influence, critical reception, and debates about the scientific and cultural status of psychoanalysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical significance and stature
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments of Freud's relative historical importance and intellectual stature (e.g., claims that Marx was 'far more historically important' and 'a finer thinker', contrasted with views that Freud permanently changed the way human nature is understood).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how transformative the subject's ideas were for subsequent thought and culture; compare influence across disciplines and time. Examples in text: Fromm credits Freud with permanently changing the understanding of human nature; Robinson calls Freud a revolutionary on par with Marx for his century. Consider both breadth (how widely influential) and depth (lasting conceptual change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific status / empirical rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether psychoanalysis qualifies as a science: critiques that Freud's 'years of intensive clinical experience' do not equate to scientific rigor; references to Popper, Grünbaum, and others who challenge psychoanalysis' falsifiability and epistemic foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge on criteria such as empirical testability, methodological transparency, replicability, and use of controlled studies. The entry cites work critiquing Freud as pseudoscientific and notes large literatures both defending and attacking scientific credibility (e.g., Fisher & Greenberg; Popper; Grünbaum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological testability and empirical support
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which Freudian hypotheses have been subjected to empirical tests (e.g., studies testing the repression hypothesis; reviews of scientific reappraisal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider availability and quality of controlled empirical studies, meta-analyses, and attempts to operationalize Freudian constructs. The page references empirical tests (Lambert et al.; Depue et al.), and books assessing Freud's theories scientifically (Fisher & Greenberg, Kline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic/clinical efficacy and relevance to psychiatry
rubrics_metrics.description: How psychoanalysis has influenced psychiatric and psychotherapeutic practice and whether it remains clinically useful (references to psychiatry literature asserting some tenets remain central).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess actual clinical outcomes, integration with mainstream psychiatric practice, and continuing educational/clinical uptake (e.g., citations to Sadock & Sadock; Michels). Note historical shifts in the relationship between psychoanalysis and psychiatry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical coherence and compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Compatibility or opposition between Freud's ideas and various philosophical positions — e.g., Sartre's critique that consciousness is essentially self-conscious; Adorno's placement of Freud opposite Husserl; Derrida's view of Freud as precursor to his radicalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate conceptual coherence when Freud is read alongside phenomenology, existentialism, hermeneutics, deconstruction, or other philosophical systems. The entry records both adaptations (Sartre's 'existential psychoanalysis') and oppositions (Adorno/Husserl).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermeneutic / interpretive contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Freud's role as progenitor of a shift from objectifying empiricism to an emphasis on subjectivity and interpretation (Ricoeur, Habermas — a 'hermeneutic version of Freud').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure contribution to interpretive methods in the humanities and social sciences: does the theory enable new modes of interpretation of texts, culture, and subjectivity? The article cites Ricoeur/Habermas on Freud's hermeneutic significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical utility and adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: The usefulness of Freudian concepts across other theoretical frameworks (e.g., Althusser's borrowing of overdetermination; Lyotard's reworking of unconscious/dream-work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether core concepts are generative and adaptable for further theoretical development in other traditions (Marxist theory, postmodernism, Lacanian reinterpretations). Examples show both appropriation and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of dreams and originality of core concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of Freudian accounts such as the dream-work, Oedipus complex, and structural models of the psyche; debates about whether Freud's accounts invert or echo earlier thinkers (e.g., parallels/inversions with Plato).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge conceptual novelty, coherence, and explanatory reach of specific doctrines (dream theory, id/ego/superego). The entry records contrasting readings (Gellner on Plato; Lyotard on dream-work reversal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideological/political critique and corruption of the movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that psychoanalysis (or its institutions) became ideologically corrupted or compromised early on (Deleuze & Guattari compare psychoanalysis to the Russian Revolution becoming corrupted; other references to factionalism within psychoanalytic societies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess institutional history and political dynamics: schisms, dogmatism, use as ideological apparatus. Consider historical episodes (society splits, enforced choices between schools) and theoretical critiques of 'corruption' or idealism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender sensitivity and feminist critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Feminist criticisms that Freud's theories reflect male-centered biases (e.g., charge of 'original superiority' for males, penis envy, Victorian views of women), alongside feminist appropriations and defenses (Mitchell's defense; Kristeva, Irigaray, Chodorow's alternative accounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate on whether theories account for social/cultural formation of gender, whether they naturalize gender hierarchies, and how interpreters have revised or used Freud to address sexual difference. Note debates between critics and defenders (Firestone, Friedan, Mitchell, Gallop).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical implications and capacity to ground ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether psychoanalytic theories can serve as a basis for ethical systems: Bernard Williams argues psychoanalytic theories may embed ethical thought and so are ill-suited as independent foundations for ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether theoretical claims about human nature logically support normative claims, or whether they presuppose ethical notions (i.e., circularity). Consider instances where psychoanalytic practice assumes ethical premises while providing individual benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary and cultural influence versus scientific claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of Freud's contribution to literature and criticism (Harold Bloom, Camille Paglia) and the argument that Freud's writings function as art or cultural discourse rather than empirical science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish influence on arts/humanities from empirical validity. Gauge value as interpretive/literary resource even if scientific credentials are contested; Paglia exemplifies seeing Freud as literary/psychological artist rather than natural scientist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with neuroscience / contemporary scientific trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Debates about bringing psychoanalysis into dialogue with neuroscience (neuropsychoanalysis) and criticisms that such moves contain fallacies or harm psychoanalytic discourse (Blass & Carmeli; Kandel's endorsement of biological engagement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate quality of interdisciplinary integration: conceptual clarity, avoidance of category errors, empirical benefits, and impact on psychoanalytic practice. The entry cites both supportive (Kandel) and critical (Blass & Carmeli) perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical accuracy and historiography of psychoanalytic episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about historical claims in Freud's accounts (e.g., seduction theory episode) and subsequent historiographical reassessments and critiques (Masson, Esterson, Schimek).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess primary evidence, archival work, and reliability of historical narratives; consider whether reinterpretations change evaluation of theoretical claims. The article cites extensive historiographical debate and literature.
